thread:
jamie: noticing a spike in scale-down failures across eu-west yesterday evening. CA kept marking nodes as unremovable; logs show a bunch of drain timeouts and liveness probe evictions. anyone seen similar?

jamie: excerpt from autoscaler logs: `I0328 19:11:05.123456 1 scale_down.go:345] Node pool/gpu-pool-1: node/node-123 failed to drain: pod "model-server-abc" evicted by liveness probe, drain timeout`

sanjay: ugh. sounds like drains are getting blocked by pods that have short-lived liveness checks or heavy preStop hooks. are we still using `--scale-down-unneeded-time=10m`?

jamie: yes default 10m. also `--scale-down-unready-time=20m` in our deployment. we saw many nodes go NotReady for 2-4m while kube-proxy + cni restarted, and CA treats those as unremovable for the unready time window.

evan: two knobs we usually tweak for noisy clusters: raise `--scale-down-unready-time` to ~30m to avoid thrashing from transient NotReady, and increase `--max-graceful-termination-sec` used by CA during drain (we set that to 300s for cpu pools but gpu pods sometimes need more). also consider `--skip-nodes-with-system-pods=false` if we want CA to try draining nodes with daemonsets.

olivia: costly tradeoff though — longer unready time = more idle GPU minutes. if we tune that up, we should pair with tighter `--scale-down-utilization-threshold` and use `balance-similar-node-groups` to consolidate. otherwise cost goes up.

jamie: noted. the cluster saw ~6 nodes idle for ~12 minutes each — that's a non-trivial hourly burn.

evan: have we tried switching expander from `most-pods` to `least-waste`? `most-pods` favors spreading which increases packing inefficiency and later makes scale-down struggle. `least-waste` tends to pack and reduce leftover fractional CPU/GPU that block deletion.

sanjay: +1 to least-waste for high-cost gpu pools. also add `--balance-similar-node-groups=true` so CA prefers shuffling instead of creating new nodegroups. we used that combo successfully in staging.

olivia: second thought — some model containers fail their readiness during drain because they re-open heavy mmap files and cause liveness flaps. We should work with infra/ML to add a short `preStop` sleep and adjust pod-level `terminationGracePeriodSeconds`. that will make drains smoother.

jamie: there's also a recurring pattern where scale-down tries to delete 3 nodes simultaneously (bulk delete) and saturates cloud API, leading to partial failures. CA has `--max-empty-bulk-delete`/`--max-graceful-termination-secs`? anyone remember exact flag?

taylor: CA flag is `--max-empty-bulk-delete` (default 10 iirc) and `--max-node-provision-time`. For deletion concurrency we tune `--max-node-termination-in-progress=2` on our heavy regions to avoid API throttling. You can simulate with the CA simulator: `./ca-simulator --config test.yaml --scenario drain-heavy` which reproduces the partial-delete pattern.

ci-bot: deploybot: canary autoscaler change applied to eu-west-canary at 2026-03-17T02:00Z — flags: `--expander=least-waste --scale-down-unready-time=30m --balance-similar-node-groups=true --max-node-termination-in-progress=2`. Monitoring heartbeat: OK.

jamie: good. can we run a short experiment next maintenance window: apply canary flags to one GPU nodepool, run a soak test with synthetic job burst, and measure (1) time nodes idle before deletion, (2) number of drain timeouts, (3) extra GPU-minutes burned?

sanjay: I'll own the experiment. plan: 90m window, synthetic k8s job that schedules 8 GPU pods for 10m bursts every 5m, run before/after with old vs new flags. will collect CA logs and node deletion traces.

olivia: add a metric to console dashboard: `autoscaler.drain_timeouts` + `gpupool.idle_minutes`. Also export `k8s.pdb.blocked_drains` from cluster exporter.

evan: if results look good, roll to eu-west and then us-west. otherwise fallback to previous config via canary rollback. :+1:

jamie: thanks team. action items: sanjay to run canary test, olivia to add dashboard tiles, evan to confirm expander change doesn't regress other pools. reopen thread with results. :thinking:
